title: Midnight latch rollout cheatsheet and hour-by-hour canvas
body:
Purpose:
Quick, compact operational checklist and hourly readout plan for a late-night / midnight-latch rollout. Designed to be used by the on-call release conductor and the night shift crew. Not exhaustive — this is a lightweight field guide for the first 6–8 hours after cutover.

Context:
- Target: Hosted API model routing change (traffic split: base-model -> variant-v2)
- Window: 2026-10-06 00:00 UTC -> 2026-10-06 08:00 UTC (primary latch at 00:10 UTC)
- Expected impact: micro-latency delta, potential warm cache churn for first 10k requests
- Why midnight: lower traffic footprint in EMEA/APAC, easier panic rollback if things trend bad for NA morning.

Quick contacts (pager-first):
- Release conductor (primary): Priya Menon (pager: SIG-Priya, slack: #re-rollouts)
- SRE lead: Jordan Lee (pager: SIG-Jordan, slack: #sre-runbook)
- Serving runtime owner: Carlos Nguyen (pager: SIG-Carlos, slack: #serving-runtime)
- Telemetry/observability: Samira Khan (pager: SIG-Samira, slack: #observability)
- Exec on-call (for escalation): Evan Brooks (pager: SIG-Evan)

Channels:
- Primary comm: Slack channel #release-midnight-latch (create ephemeral thread for notes)
- Incident channel: #inc-releases (use only if rollback/major incident)
- Voice: Zoom impromptu link (start when >2 simultaneous SEV signals)

Pre-latch (T-120 -> T-10 minutes) checklist (do not skip):
- [ ] Confirm feature-flag gating is staged and can be toggled from console (console v3.4.1).
- [ ] Verify canary traffic endpoint healthy (GET /health on variant-v2) from three regions.
- [ ] Confirm autoscaler warm pool sizes for dedicated GPU fleets (allocation >= 30% reserve).
- [ ] Snapshot deployment configuration and commit hash for rollback reference (commit: 0a9f3b4).
- [ ] Push exact runbook link into #release-midnight-latch and pin first message.
- [ ] Ensure logging retention set to verbose for next 2 hours (Samira to flip sampling).
- [ ] Confirm alert routing: latency P95 > 1200ms -> page SRE, error spike >2% -> page release conductor.
- [ ] Sanity smoke: run short prompts through variant-v2 (3x) and validate tokenized output length and no-timeouts.
- [ ] Backup: start temporary request-replay buffer (for forensic replay if needed).
- [ ] Annotate expected KPIs and thresholds in the pinned message (see "Kill thresholds" below).

Midnight latch timeline (hour-by-hour, owner initials):
- 00:00 UTC (Priya): Flip feature-flag to route 1% of traffic to variant-v2. Post live note + small sample outputs.
- 00:05 UTC (Jordan): Check infra telemetry (node util, queue depth, GPU mem) for anomalous jump.
- 00:10 UTC (Priya): Increase to 10% if metrics good for first 5 minutes.
- 00:20 UTC (Samira): Validate observability dashboards — latency P50/P95, error rate, token cost.
- 00:30 UTC (Carlos): Warm caches and confirm KV cache hit-rate trend. Re-provision warm pool if miss spike > 15%.
- 00:45 UTC (Evan): Cross-check user-facing metrics (API success rate, throughput).
- 01:00 UTC (Priya/Jordan): Decide on continued ramp to 50% or hold. Document reason in thread.
- 02:00 UTC (All): Decision gate: continue to 100% or partial rollback to 5% and pause for deeper forensics.
- 03:30 UTC (Telemetry lead): If at 100% for 90m with stable metrics, reduce verbose logging and revert sampling to normal.
- 04:00 UTC (Ops): Prepare morning handoff summary (short bullets) for AM shift.

Kill thresholds (immediate rollback if any are triggered):
- Latency: P95 increase > 2x baseline sustained for 5 minutes.
- Errors: 5xx spike > 3% absolute for 3 continuous minutes.
- Resource: GPU OOMs observed on any node (automated alarm -> immediate mitigation).
- Data correctness: detected invalid structured outputs (schema mismatch) in >0.1% of sampled requests.

Rollback procedure (rapid):
- [ ] Toggle feature-flag to route 0% to variant-v2 (Priya) — this is immediate emergency rollback.
- [ ] Cut verbose logs to normal (Samira) only after rollback confirmed.
- [ ] Run lightweight replay from buffer for quick repro attempt (Carlos) — capture first 500 failed requests.
- [ ] Create SEV ticket in JIRA (JIRA-RELEASE-1124) and assign to on-call SRE + serving runtime owner.
- [ ] Postmortem owner assigned within 24h if rollback occurred.

Telemetry & dashboards to watch (live):
- Release pulse view (P50/P95, error %, QPS) — pinned link
- Node-level heatmap (CPU/GPU mem/IO) — monitor for hotspots
- Latency distribution (token build vs backend overhead)
- Auth/signature errors (edge case) — small but high-impact
- Output-quality sampling: run 200 golden prompt checks every 15 minutes during ramp

Smoke test prompts (short list — run 3x each):
- Summarize: "Summarize the following paragraph in 20 words or less:" (checks truncation)
- Code assist: small python function generate + run lint (checks for malformed code emitted)
- Safety: content moderation quick checks (should be allowed neutral content)
- Embedding consistency: ensure embedding vectors length unchanged (sanity vector dims)

Night-shift heuristics / notes to conductor (informal):
- Be conservative in first 45 minutes; transient noise common when caches refill.
- If multiple small signals appear (latency + small error bump + memory drift) treat as composite -> pause ramp.
- Keep direct comm lines open; escalate early. Better to pause than to roll forward blind.
- Use the pinned slack thread for every decision (time-stamped).

Open questions / TODOs (sticking points to resolve pre-latch):
- Who is owner for content-quality gating automation? (Samira suggested a lightweight scripts run; needs signoff.)
- Confirm if dedicated fleet warm-pools are charged under reserved capacity during short bursts — finance ops impact.
- Add small synthetic that triggers known edge-case in parser v1.9 (we have a mocked sample, need to add to smoke set).

Post-latch handoff (format for morning summary):
- Short header: Rollout start time, final traffic %, rollback? (Y/N)
- Key signals: P95 delta, error delta, notable infra events
- Forensics pointers: link to replay buffer + top 20 failed request ids
- Action items: triage owners + ETA

Appendix (quick snippets):
- Useful commands:
  - curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/generate -H 'X-RW-Env: staging' -d '{"model":"variant-v2","prompt":"hello"}'
  - k get pods -l app=serving-runtime -o wide (watch for node restarts)
- Incident logging template (post in JIRA): one-line summary, chronological bullets, impact estimate, mitigation steps

Notes to self: this doc is intentionally compact. Keep it pinned during run. If we need a full runbook, convert to the canonical Deployment Runbooks space after the fact.

-- E.B. (initial sketch)
